newsitem.title: MEXICO: Banco de Mexico reserves, assets rise to Oct 31.
newsitem.headline: Banco de Mexico reserves, assets rise to Oct 31.

text.p: Banco de Mexico said Monday its net international assets as of October 31, 1996, were $4.457 billion, compared with $3.872 billion on October 25.
The central bank said that its net international reserves as of October 31 were $16.094 billion, compared with $15.763 billion as of October 25.
It attributed the increase in international assets to:
- Net revenues from operations with state oil firm Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) worth $763 million
- Net sales of foreign currency to the federal government worth $211 million to cover external debt service

- A net gain of $33 million for a combination of factors including changes in the dollar value of dollar assets and liabilities held by the bank; net returns on interest rates for trading of metals and securities; and net deposits in dollar accounts of commercial banks at the central bank.

Banco de Mexico said the monetary base rose 3.531 billion pesos due to seasonal demand for notes and coins stemming from salary payments for the second two weeks of October and November 1 Day of the Dead celebrations.
The balance of the government's deposits with the central bank rose by a net 4.490 billion pesos, due mainly to reception of taxes.

Central bank credit to financial institutions rose by 6.027 billion pesos to meet the rising demand for notes and coins and to compensate for lesser liquidity caused by the increase in government deposits at the central bank.
The following tables detail Banco de Mexico's assets and net domestic credit. All figures are in billions of pesos, unless otherwise indicated.

*Net International Assets are defined as gross international assets minus central bank liabilities with the IMF and assets of less than a six month duration from other central banks. --Martin Langfield, Mexico City newsroom +525 7289558
